Subject: Next steps & environment checklist — Quickstart for NovaClient POC

Hi Amit / Elena —

Thanks again for the quick demo earlier. This thread is a short recap + proposed checklist for the POC onramp so we can get a small local pilot running (Python first, add TypeScript samples if helpful). Please read and flag anything missing or off-priority.

Top-level asks / scope (POC):
- Run a local sample app that exercises: authentication, generation (structured output), tool-calling stub, and embeddings + a reranker.
- Start with Python sample + Docker compose for local reproducibility; add TS example as a follow-up.
- Keep PII/data off the POC dataset; we'll provide synthetic prompts.

Proposed quickstart checklist (attachments + links below):
1) Access: HubSpot deal & test API key (Scoped, short-lived) — we can issue a POC key for NovaClient.
2) SDK: Pull SDK-samples repo (linked in related_links).
3) Env variables: REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_ENV (region alias), LOCAL_RERANK_PATH.
4) Local infra: docker-compose with Redis (for session state), a minimal FAISS container for embeddings index.
5) Auth choices: API key for now; we can swap to OIDC for Dedicated later.
6) Routing: model aliasing config to route low-cost baseline vs higher-quality generating model for critical paths.
7) Structured output/tool calling: sample tool schema + a small tool stub in the sample app to demonstrate function-like outputs.
8) Embeddings & reranker: sample dataset, embed dimension note, and a small local reranker using dot-product with FAISS.

Next steps I suggest:
- Confirm Python first (yes/no) and any firm blackout windows for infra tests.
- 45-minute technical workshop (we can do Wed/Thu next week) where Karthik will walk the team through repo and run the Docker compose.
- I attached a one-page checklist and the sample tarball of the app to this message.

Thanks — happy to adapt.

Best,

Naomi / team — looping in some technical notes below (responding inline to Amit's asks). Quoted Amit for context:

> "For the embeddings/reranker: we'd like the sample to show end-to-end query -> embed -> local index -> rerank results so our search team can validate."

Totally — here's a concise plan I will deliver in the sample app:
- Repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-samples (branch: novaclient-poc).
- Docker compose: will spin up the sample app (python), Redis, and a lightweight FAISS service. The sample includes a script seed_index.py to pre-seed ~250 synthetic items (JSONL).
- Embedding vector dims: we will ship with 1536-d default (open models), plus a configurable flag (EMBED_DIM) if you want 1024/2048. README will call out tradeoffs.
- Pre-seeded index: small pickled FAISS index included in repo for fast start; seed script included to rebuild.
- Reranker: simple two-stage flow (retriever -> embed -> dot-product rerank). We'll include a small eval harness so NovaClient can plug in own query set.

> "Please include a one-paragraph data flow note (what hits Redwood, what stays local)."

Data flow (short):
- Inputs: queries/prompts are sent to Redwood's hosted inference via the SDK when using the hosted POC key. Embeddings may be computed locally (if you run an OSS embedder) or via Redwood; sample app includes both options toggled by USE_LOCAL_EMB=true/false.
- Local-only: the FAISS index and any persisted document store remain in your local container; we will not persist prompts to external storage unless you enable REDWOOD_LOGGING=true.
- PII: sample scripts will mask fields and use synthetic data by default.

Auth & test creds: for POC we recommend API keys scoped to a sandbox project (short TTL). OIDC integration is tracked as a follow-on.

Structured output & tool calling:
- The sample uses a small tool spec (tools/lookup.py) that demonstrates function-like returns (JSON schema) and a verification harness. We'll include a TypeScript stub in /ts-samples.

Routing note:
- For the POC we will use model-alias routing (config/route.yaml) to demonstrate fallback to a faster, cheaper model under load. We'll include comments on when to prefer cache+batching vs synchronous low-latency.

I'll drop the docker-compose file and the seed index into the branch today and notify when ready.

Karthik Iyer
